## Problem Statement

New users face a blank platform: the first workbench, first pipeline, and first
model deployment all start from empty forms, and time-to-first-success is
measured in days. We want a curated tutorial gallery in the Dashboard — a set
of maintained, tested tutorials (notebooks and pipelines) that users can launch
into their own project with one click. This requires product code (the gallery
and launch mechanics), authored content (the tutorials themselves), and
documentation — three different kinds of work with different owners and review
processes.

## High-Level Requirements

| ID | Priority | Requirement |
|-------|----------|-------------|
| HLR-1 | P0 | The Dashboard has a tutorial gallery from which a user can launch a tutorial into their project (opening a workbench with the notebook, or importing the pipeline). |
| HLR-2 | P0 | Six curated tutorials exist covering the core journeys: first workbench, data prep, first training run, first pipeline, first deployment, first RAG app. Each is tested against the current release. |
| HLR-3 | P1 | A tutorial packaging format (metadata, pinned images, validation manifest) is defined so tutorials are versioned and testable independently of Dashboard releases. |
| HLR-4 | P2 | Documentation covers using the gallery and the contribution process for new tutorials. |

## Affected Components

- Dashboard
- Notebooks
- Data Science Pipelines
- Documentation

## Out of Scope

- Partner- or community-contributed tutorial intake (contribution process is
  documented, but no submission tooling this release)
- Localization of tutorial content

## Open Questions

None.

# Tutorial packaging format (metadata, pinned images, validation manifest)

## Description

This epic defines the tutorial packaging format that makes tutorials versioned and testable artifacts independent of Dashboard releases. It produces the format specification and the validation means for tutorial packages: the metadata that describes a tutorial, the pinning of the images a tutorial runs on, and a validation manifest against which a packaged tutorial can be mechanically checked.

## Scope

- Define the tutorial packaging format covering:
  - Tutorial metadata (identity, journey description, kind: notebook-based or pipeline-based, and the fields a consuming UI needs to present and launch it)
  - Pinned images: how the notebook/workbench image (and any other images the tutorial depends on) are pinned so a tutorial runs reproducibly
  - Validation manifest: the machine-checkable description of what a packaged tutorial must satisfy to be considered valid and testable
- Define format versioning so tutorial packages can evolve and be tested independently of Dashboard releases
- Provide the validation means by which a tutorial package is checked against the format (validation manifest is passed/fail-checkable without a Dashboard release)
- Ensure the format covers both tutorial kinds named by the strategy: notebook-based tutorials (launched by opening a workbench with the notebook) and pipeline-based tutorials (launched by importing the pipeline)

## Acceptance Criteria

- The packaging format specification defines tutorial metadata, image pinning, and a validation manifest, satisfying the elements named in HLR-3.
- A tutorial packaged per the format can be validated mechanically by checking it against its validation manifest, with no Dashboard release involved in the check.
- The format carries a version, and a packaged tutorial declares the format version it targets, so tutorials are versioned independently of Dashboard releases.
- The format supports both a notebook-based tutorial and a pipeline-based tutorial (demonstrated by a minimal exemplar package of each kind that passes validation).

## HLR Traceability

- **HLR-3 (P1)** — full coverage. The tutorial packaging format (metadata, pinned images, validation manifest) is this epic's deliverable; tutorials become versioned and testable independently of Dashboard releases.
- This epic also enables HLR-1 and HLR-2 (both P0), which build on the format; priority is inherited as P0 accordingly.

# Dashboard tutorial gallery with one-click launch into a project

## Description

This epic delivers the tutorial gallery in the Dashboard: a curated gallery surface from which a user can launch a tutorial into their own project with one click — opening a workbench containing the tutorial notebook, or importing the tutorial pipeline. This is the product-code work stream of the strategy, owned by the Dashboard team.

## Scope

- Add a tutorial gallery surface to the Dashboard that lists available curated tutorials, driven by tutorial package metadata
- One-click launch of a notebook-based tutorial into the user's project: creating/opening a workbench with the tutorial's notebook, using the images pinned by the tutorial package
- One-click launch of a pipeline-based tutorial into the user's project: importing the tutorial's pipeline
- Consume the tutorial packaging format (metadata, pinned images, validation manifest) defined by this strategy so the gallery presents and launches any package conforming to that format
- Consistency with existing Dashboard patterns for project-scoped resource creation (the Dashboard reads and writes the platform's Kubernetes resources; it owns no data plane)

## Acceptance Criteria

- The Dashboard shows a tutorial gallery listing available curated tutorials with their metadata.
- From the gallery, a user can launch a tutorial into their own project with one click by opening a workbench containing the tutorial notebook.
- From the gallery, a user can launch a pipeline tutorial into their own project with one click by importing the pipeline.
- Launching a tutorial packaged in the defined tutorial packaging format succeeds end-to-end in a real project — verified with at least one tutorial from the curated set or an equivalent package conforming to the format.
- The Dashboard's existing build/CI pipeline remains green with the gallery changes.

## HLR Traceability

- **HLR-1 (P0)** — full coverage. The tutorial gallery in the Dashboard and the one-click launch mechanics (workbench with notebook, pipeline import) are this epic's deliverable.

# Document the tutorial gallery and the tutorial contribution process

## Description

This epic delivers the documentation for the tutorial gallery: using the gallery (browsing and launching tutorials into a project) and the contribution process for new tutorials. It is the documentation work stream of the strategy and runs after the implementations so the docs describe what was built. Submission tooling for community/partner contributions is out of scope this release — the contribution process is documented as a process only.

## Scope

Content outline (inside the Red Hat docs content process):

- **Using the tutorial gallery** (new topic): what the gallery is, browsing available curated tutorials, launching a notebook tutorial into a project (workbench with the notebook), launching a pipeline tutorial (pipeline import), and what the user should see at each step of a first journey
- **Contributing a new tutorial** (new topic): the contribution process for new tutorials — packaging a tutorial per the tutorial packaging format (metadata, pinned images, validation manifest), validating it against its manifest, and the review path for curated content; explicitly scoped to process documentation with no submission tooling this release
- Cross-reference updates in existing getting-started/onboarding documentation where the gallery changes the recommended first-run path (incidental reference updates that fall out of the new topics)

## Acceptance Criteria

- A documentation topic covers using the tutorial gallery: browsing curated tutorials and launching a notebook tutorial and a pipeline tutorial into a project.
- A documentation topic covers the contribution process for new tutorials, including packaging per the tutorial packaging format and validation against the manifest, and states that submission tooling is not available this release.
- The content is technically reviewed against the implemented gallery, tutorials, and packaging format (reviewed by or with the implementing teams).
- Documentation builds pass in the docs toolchain.

## HLR Traceability

- **HLR-4 (P2)** — full coverage. Documentation of gallery usage and the tutorial contribution process is this epic's deliverable. (Priority is P1 via the docs-authoring exception from the strategy's Major priority, not inherited from the P0 implementations.)

## DAG Justification

| Edge | Rule | Rationale |
|------|------|-----------|
| E001 → E002 | Rule 13 (build-against artifact) | The Dashboard gallery code builds against the packaging format — it parses tutorial metadata and the validation manifest and uses pinned images to launch tutorials. The format/schema must exist before the consuming code is written. |
| E001 → E003 | Rule 13 (build-against artifact) | The notebook tutorials are packaged to the format (metadata, pinned images, validation manifest); packaging cannot start before the format is defined. |
| E001 → E004 | Rule 13 (build-against artifact) | The pipeline tutorial is packaged to the same format. |

| E004 → E005 | Rule 11 (docs-authoring last) | Docs describe the built tutorials and contribution process. |

**Parallel non-edges (deliberate):**

- **E002 ∥ E003 ∥ E004** — the gallery (Dashboard repo) and the tutorial content (notebook and pipeline artifacts) live in different repos/components with no shared build artifacts. The gallery consumes tutorials as *content* at runtime, not as a build-against artifact; per Rule 13's configuration/content distinction this coupling is expressed as an acceptance criterion on the gallery epic ("launching a tutorial packaged in the defined format succeeds end-to-end, verified with at least one tutorial from the curated set or an equivalent fixture"), never as a DAG edge. Edges here would serialize three independently staffed work streams.
- **E003 ∥ E004** — different components and teams (Notebooks/Workbenches vs. Data Science Pipelines/RHOAI Pipelines); the tutorial split follows the component boundary, and the two content sets share only the packaging format contract, which E001 provides to both.

## Health Warnings

- **Missing strategy sections** (non-blocking): the strategy has no Impacted Teams table, no Dependencies table, no Given/When/Then Acceptance Criteria, no Non-Functional Requirements, and no Technical Approach / Staff Engineer Input. Decomposition proceeded from the HLR table, affected components list, and problem statement. Epic acceptance criteria were derived at the functional level of the HLRs.
- **Team inference**: owner teams were taken from `.context/architecture-context/` owning-team fields (Dashboard → RHOAI Dashboard; Notebooks → Workbenches; Data Science Pipelines → RHOAI Pipelines). No architecture-context file exists for the Documentation component; E005's team (`RHOAI Documentation`) is inferred from the strategy's statement that documentation is a separately owned work stream — verify with the actual docs team before scheduling.
- **E001 component mapping** (non-obvious): the packaging format spans Notebooks and Data Science Pipelines content and is consumed by Dashboard code. Assigned the single most-relevant canonical component `Notebooks` (tutorials are primarily notebook artifacts, and the format exists to keep them independent of Dashboard releases); the span is noted here per the component-name constraint.
- **Scope trap — tutorial maintenance**: HLR-2 requires tutorials "tested against the current release" and the problem statement calls them "maintained" tutorials, but the strategy scopes no ongoing re-validation process for future releases and the out-of-scope list does not address it. Recurring per-release re-testing effort is unplanned; the validation manifest from the packaging format mitigates but does not eliminate it.
